Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International.text: It began in 1925 on a rent-free lease of an abandoned auto racetrack, The Atlanta Speedway.
Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International.evidence: Hartsfield–Jackson began with a five-year, rent-free lease on 287 acres (116 ha) that was an abandoned auto racetrack named The Atlanta Speedway. The lease was signed on April 16, 1925, by Mayor Walter Sims, who committed the city to develop it into an airfield.

Dubai International Airport.text: Its Terminal 3 is the largest airport terminal in the world and the fourth-largest building by floor space.
Dubai International Airport.evidence: Terminal 3 is the fourth-largest building in the world by floor space and the largest airport terminal in the world.

Tokyo Haneda Airport.text: From 1978 to 2010 it handled almost all of Tokyo's domestic flights, leaving most long-haul ones to Narita.
Tokyo Haneda Airport.evidence: from 1978 to 2010, Haneda handled almost all domestic flights to and from Tokyo as well as "scheduled charter" flights to a small number of major cities in East and Southeast Asia, while Narita handled the vast majority of international flights from further locations.

Dallas Fort Worth International Airport.text: The airport has its own police, fire protection and emergency medical services.
Dallas Fort Worth International Airport.evidence: It has its own police, fire protection, and emergency medical services.

Shanghai Pudong International Airport.text: It is also the world's second-busiest airport by cargo traffic.
Shanghai Pudong International Airport.evidence: With 3,778,331 metric tons handled in 2024, the airport is the world's second-busiest airport by cargo traffic.

O'Hare International Airport.text: It has eight runways, the most of any airport in the world.
O'Hare International Airport.evidence: It has eight runways, the most of any airport in the world.

Heathrow Airport.text: In the 1950s it had six runways, arranged in three pairs in the shape of a hexagram.
Heathrow Airport.evidence: In the 1950s, Heathrow had six runways, arranged in three pairs at different angles in the shape of a hexagram

Istanbul Airport.text: On 6 April 2019 all scheduled passenger flights moved here from Atatürk Airport, along with the code IST.
Istanbul Airport.evidence: All scheduled commercial passenger flights were transferred from Atatürk Airport to Istanbul Airport on 6 April 2019, following the closure of Atatürk Airport for scheduled passenger flights. The IATA airport code IST was also transferred to the new airport.

Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport.text: Its code, CAN, comes from Canton, the historical romanization of Guangzhou.
Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport.evidence: The airport codes were inherited from the former Baiyun Airport, and the IATA code is derived from Guangzhou's historical romanization Canton.

Denver International Airport.text: Its 16,000 ft runway is the longest public use runway in North America.
Denver International Airport.evidence: Runway 16R/34L, with a length of 16000 ft (4877 m), is the longest public use runway in North America and the fifth longest in the world.
